title: Portfolio Projects
summary: Build evidence that shows how you observe movement, explain choices, protect safety boundaries, and improve a plan over time.

sections.title: Project Ladder
sections.summary: Start with narrow projects that can be finished, reviewed, and improved.
items: Movement screen write-up with observed patterns, education-only findings, and referral boundaries
Warmup progression for one sport, activity, or joint pattern
Technique breakdown using public movement principles and cited learning sources
Training log dashboard with readiness, RPE, attendance, and reflection fields
Career case study comparing education path, work setting, credentials, and company role
actions: Choose one audience and one movement problem before selecting tools
Record the goal, inputs, method, limits, and what changed after review
Add a short ethics note that states what was observed and what was not concluded
outputs: Reflection section with next learning step

sections.title: Evidence Quality
sections.summary: A strong portfolio makes the reasoning easy to inspect.
items: Goal, audience, method, safety boundaries, and referral rules
Before and after plan changes with dates or session markers
Observed data separated from interpretation
Clear citation or source notes for educational concepts
Communication reflection for athlete, parent, coach, clinician, or customer
actions: Review each project for scope language before sharing
Keep private health details out of public work unless consent and policy allow it
Replace vague claims with observed facts and learning outcomes

sections.title: Role Matching
sections.summary: Shape projects toward the role you want next.
items: Clinical and rehab paths: observation logs, exercise progressions, communication reflections
Strength and performance paths: program design, testing summaries, cue libraries
Research and data paths: small datasets, analysis notebooks, visualizations, literature summaries
Technology paths: product requirements, data flow diagrams, QA notes, user education screens
Education paths: lesson plans, student progress measures, inclusive activity adaptations
actions: Attach each project to a career path and a school roadmap level
Identify the mentor or reviewer who can validate quality
Keep the project small enough to finish and improve

checklists.title: Ready To Share
items: Title explains the project without hype
Scope boundary is visible
Methods and data are described plainly
Every chart, screenshot, or claim has context
Next step shows learning and humility

title: Business Models
summary: Movement science can become a local service, clinical pathway, school program, lab service, education product, or software company when the audience and scope are specific.

sections.title: Service Models
sections.summary: Service businesses win through trust, repeatable operations, and measurable learning.
items: Physical therapy, occupational therapy, or sports medicine clinic ownership through licensed practice
Sports performance studio for youth, high school, college, or adult athletes
Mobile movement education and screening service within credential boundaries
School-based kinesiology, wellness, or career education program
Corporate wellness and movement-readiness education program
actions: Define the buyer, user, setting, and safety boundary
Write one intake, one session flow, and one follow-up process
List credential requirements before offering any health-related service

sections.title: Technology Models
sections.summary: Technology models need a narrow workflow, trusted data handling, and a real user problem.
items: Biomechanics lab or motion-analysis service
Wearable-data interpretation and education platform
Coach workflow tool for readiness, reports, and progress tracking
Movement education content library or credential pathway
Clinical operations product for intake, outcomes, or patient education
actions: Map input data, Core processing, rendered output, and storage boundaries
Keep early product scope to one repeated job
Verify privacy, consent, and professional boundary requirements

sections.title: Revenue And Operations
sections.summary: A business model is stronger when delivery, pricing, support, and quality control are visible.
items: One-time assessment, recurring coaching, group program, school contract, clinic license, or subscription
Scheduling, intake, payment, records, reporting, and support process
Quality review cadence for content, coaches, reports, and customer outcomes
Partnership channels through clinics, schools, teams, employers, and community organizations
actions: Choose one primary revenue path first
Document what the business will refuse to do outside scope
Create a weekly operations checklist before scaling

checklists.title: Business Readiness
items: Specific audience
Specific movement education problem
Credential and referral rules
Repeatable service or product workflow
Evidence and privacy policy

title: Skills Builder
summary: Movement science careers combine anatomy, observation, coaching, data, communication, ethics, and role-specific tools.

sections.title: Foundation Stack
sections.summary: These skills support almost every movement science path.
items: Anatomy, joint actions, tissue basics, and movement vocabulary
Biomechanics, force, timing, balance, posture, and coordination concepts
Exercise physiology, adaptation, fatigue, recovery, and progression
Program design for warmup, strength, mobility, return-to-activity, or education
Communication with athletes, patients, parents, coaches, clinicians, and customers
actions: Practice explaining one concept in student, parent, and coach language
Use one movement video to identify what is visible and what is unknown
Create one progression with easier, normal, and harder levels

sections.title: Technical Stack
sections.summary: Technical skills make your work easier to inspect and easier to improve.
items: Video review and movement annotation
Spreadsheet analysis, simple statistics, and chart interpretation
Force, timing, balance, wearable, or workload data interpretation
Report writing with evidence boundaries and plain language
Privacy-aware handling of health, school, and performance information
actions: Build one spreadsheet that tracks sessions, RPE, readiness, and notes
Annotate one movement frame with visible joints and coaching cues
Write a report that separates observation from conclusion

sections.title: Professional Stack
sections.summary: Professional habits make internships, jobs, and companies safer.
items: Listening, note-taking, follow-up, and feedback loops
Referral judgment when pain, injury, illness, or medical concerns appear
Documentation that is concise, dated, and respectful
Team communication across coach, clinician, teacher, parent, and athlete roles
Ethical boundaries for claims, credentials, privacy, and customer promises
actions: Write a two-sentence referral boundary for your portfolio
Ask a mentor to review one project for clarity and scope
Turn feedback into a dated improvement note

checklists.title: Weekly Builder
items: One anatomy concept reviewed
One movement observation practiced
One communication note written
One data or chart skill practiced
One project improved

title: Certifications
summary: Certifications support readiness and supervised experience; licensure and clinical authority remain separate where required.

sections.title: Early Credentials
sections.summary: Early credentials help students become safer volunteers, interns, and assistants.
items: CPR/AED and first aid
Youth-safety or athlete-safety training when working with minors
Introductory anatomy, kinesiology, exercise science, or health science coursework
Basic coaching, officiating, or volunteer training through school or community programs
actions: Check age, cost, expiration, and renewal requirements
Save proof of completion in the career portfolio
Match each credential to a role or internship requirement

sections.title: Performance And Wellness Credentials
sections.summary: Fitness and performance credentials should match the setting, audience, and education path.
items: ACSM, NSCA, NASM, or ACE credentials for fitness and performance paths
CSCS after degree requirements are met for strength and conditioning
Specialty education in speed, mobility, corrective exercise, nutrition coaching, or youth training when relevant
Vendor training for wearable, motion capture, force plate, or coaching platforms
actions: Compare prerequisites before paying for an exam
Use certification study to build portfolio projects
Verify continuing education expectations

sections.title: Clinical And Professional Credentials
sections.summary: Clinical credentials require accredited education, supervised hours, exams, and jurisdiction rules.
items: BOC athletic training certification after accredited athletic training education
PT, PTA, OT, OTA, physician, physician assistant, nursing, and related credentials through accredited programs and boards
State licensure, renewal, continuing education, and scope of practice requirements
Clinical observation and supervised placement documentation
actions: Use official program and board sources for requirements
Track prerequisites and observation hours by school
Keep clinical language aligned with licensed scope

checklists.title: Credential Fit Check
items: Recognized by the target role
Prerequisites are met or planned
Cost and renewal are understood
Scope is clear
Evidence can be added to portfolio

title: Start a Movement Science Company
summary: Build from a clear movement problem, a specific audience, ethical boundaries, and a repeatable workflow before adding scale.

sections.title: Founder Sequence
sections.summary: A movement company starts with scope, audience, and repeatability.
items: Pick one audience: athlete, parent, coach, clinic, school, employer, or student
Define one painful movement education problem in plain language
Choose a service or product model that fits credentials and scope
Document safety boundaries, referral rules, and education-only language
Run a small paid or supervised pilot before expanding
actions: Write the problem in the customer's words
Create one-page offer, intake, delivery, and follow-up notes
Ask three target users what they already do today

sections.title: Company Building Blocks
sections.summary: The business needs a clear offer and clean operations before growth.
items: Offer: outcome the customer understands
Evidence: how movement data, education, and progress are documented
Operations: scheduling, intake, records, payments, support, and quality review
Trust: credentials, references, policies, and professional boundaries
Growth: schools, clinics, teams, employers, and community channels
actions: Map the first customer journey from discovery to renewal
Set a weekly quality review for service notes and customer feedback
Build referral relationships before claims expand

sections.title: Launch Guardrails
sections.summary: Trust comes from saying clearly what the company can and cannot do.
items: Do not diagnose, treat, or promise injury recovery outside licensed scope
Use clinician referral pathways when pain, injury, or medical concerns appear
Keep student, parent, and athlete messaging educational and transparent
Protect privacy before collecting movement, health, or school data
actions: Add scope text to intake, reports, website, and sales materials
Create referral language for medical concerns
Review privacy and consent requirements before collecting data

checklists.title: Pilot Ready
items: Audience is specific
Problem is plain
Offer can be delivered repeatedly
Safety boundaries are written
Feedback collection is ready

title: Internships
summary: Internships, observation hours, lab roles, and assistant roles turn movement science learning into verified experience.

sections.title: Entry Points
sections.summary: Use the role and setting to choose the right first experience.
items: Clinical observation in PT, OT, athletic training, or sports medicine clinics
Rehab aide, tech, front desk, or patient services work in outpatient settings
Sports performance internships with teams, schools, or training facilities
Biomechanics, exercise physiology, or motor learning lab assistant roles
Health technology internships in product, support, data, QA, or research
actions: Choose one domain and list ten matching organizations
Check official career pages and school internship offices
Track outreach, response, requirements, and follow-up dates

sections.title: Application Sequence
sections.summary: Preparation makes outreach more specific and more respectful.
items: Build a one-page resume with coursework, certifications, and movement projects
Write a short message that explains why that organization fits the path
Contact clinics, labs, teams, and companies through verified channels
Convert each interview into a learning conversation about the role
Document what was learned after every shadowing or internship day
actions: Prepare two portfolio projects before outreach
Ask about supervision, schedule, school credit, and confidentiality rules
Send a concise thank-you message after every conversation

checklists.title: Internship Readiness
items: CPR/AED started or completed when relevant
One movement project documented
One professional reference identified
Availability and transportation clarified
School-credit requirements checked

title: Application Prep
summary: Strong applications show direction, preparation, and respect for the organization before asking for an opportunity.

sections.title: Materials
sections.summary: Keep materials clear, role-specific, and evidence-backed.
items: One-page resume tailored to the domain
Short cover note explaining why that company and role fit the path
Portfolio link or PDF with two to four relevant projects
Reference list with permission from each reference
Tracker for applications, follow-ups, and outcomes
actions: Use the job or internship description to select resume bullets
Put certifications, coursework, and portfolio projects near the top when relevant
Save each version with the company and role name

sections.title: Interview Prep
sections.summary: Interview answers should connect learning, behavior, and fit.
items: Explain career direction in less than one minute
Prepare one example of coaching, helping, analyzing, or learning from feedback
Know the company category, audience, and relevant roles
Ask how students or early-career staff grow inside the organization
Prepare a boundary-aware answer for medical or injury questions outside scope
actions: Practice out loud with a timer
Write three questions for the interviewer
Send follow-up within one business day

checklists.title: Before Submit
items: Role-specific resume
No unsupported claims
Portfolio link works
Contact information checked
Follow-up date scheduled
